scope: Establish the durable item-attempt domain, schema, repository and composition foundation for DATA-02 recovery evidence.

implemented_contract: A domain-level SyncItemAttempt binds UUID run and batch identities, asset, phase, attempt number, execution token, universe hash and authority hash.
Each retry inserts a new monotonic attempt row under the stable batch lock; an active RUNNING attempt blocks a concurrent begin.
Every attempt in one batch must reuse the same frozen universe hash and authority content hash.
One attempt permits exactly one repository-owned RUNNING-to-terminal transition; later terminal rewrites fail closed.
Initial ORM inserts must be domain-valid RUNNING rows; normal model save, queryset update, bulk mutation and deletion cannot create terminal evidence or rewrite/remove history.
Explicit recovery converts stale RUNNING rows to INTERRUPTED before a later retry receives the next attempt number.
Migration 0079 adds unique batch/asset/phase/attempt identity, positive attempt-number and terminal-time constraints without a foreign key to the existing UUID control plane.
A 25-asset failure test proves durable queries are not truncated at the Celery response preview limit of 20.

resolved_before_commit: Direct ORM creation can no longer insert a terminal state and bypass the repository-owned transition.
Repository begin rejects universe-hash or authority-hash drift anywhere within one stable batch.
The new ORM remains in a separate module so the existing large-file governance ceiling is not raised.
independent_review.accepted_scope: Suitable as an additive storage foundation only; DATA-02 phase wiring and production acceptance remain open.

governance.reason: The durable store exists, while phase wiring, execution-token recovery, PostgreSQL concurrency evidence and production acceptance remain open.

remaining_repository_gates: Wire quote, valuation, price, financial and publication begin/finish outcomes into the item-attempt store.
Create the stable initial batch before attempts and carry one execution token through Celery and command retries.
Prove concurrent begin, interrupted recovery, terminal immutability and transaction rollback on PostgreSQL.
Validate provider identities before fact mutation or roll back the complete mutation on mismatch.
Produce policy-hash-bound numeric tolerance evidence for all four frozen Publications.
